group.description: Whether transitions are drawn from the kit's declared motion language rather than improvised per component, and whether they explain causality without obstructing the task.

capabilities.title: Honors reduced-motion preference
capabilities.description: Under a reduced-motion preference every transition collapses to its declared reduced behavior with no meaning lost and no lifecycle broken — and the preference is resolved by the host rather than queried by each component.

port.contract: Resolves the reduced-motion preference once at the composition root, exposes it to all descendants, and updates them when the operating-system preference changes.

capabilities.rationale: The canonical dual-facet capability named in the registry doctrine. A component both promises correct reduced behavior and depends on the host to tell it the preference; if each component queried the media feature itself the policy could not be overridden or tested.

capabilities.title: Every transition uses a declared class
capabilities.description: Each state transition the surface performs resolves to one of the kit's declared transition classes, so no component invents its own timing, easing, or animated property set.
capabilities.rationale: The mechanism that makes motion consistent by construction: a component declares a state transition and the kit's table decides how it renders. Statically checkable in part — raw duration and easing literals in source are lintable without any capture at all.

capabilities.title: Measured duration matches its token
capabilities.description: A transition's observed duration matches the duration token its class declares, so the motion language is real at runtime and not merely declared in source.
capabilities.rationale: Needs per-transition timing, which does not exist — settle timing is persisted through CaptureTargetTiming but transition measurement is not. The distinction matters: a component can reference the right token and still be overridden by a stray CSS rule.

capabilities.title: Only compositable properties animate
capabilities.description: Transitions animate transform, opacity, color, and filter only; height and width changes are expressed through clipping or a layout-difference technique rather than by tweening layout properties.
capabilities.rationale: Statically lintable from source today and confirmable from computed style at runtime. This is the rule that keeps motion from becoming a performance problem as the catalog grows.

capabilities.title: Motion never gates task completion
capabilities.description: A user can proceed with their task while any transition is running; no animation delays the availability of a control or the acceptance of input.
capabilities.rationale: DESIGN.md already requires this in every kit. It becomes enforceable rather than aspirational because no declared transition class exceeds 400ms, so a measured transition longer than its class ceiling is a finding.

capabilities.title: Nothing animates on first paint
capabilities.description: Initial render is immediate; entrance motion applies only to asynchronously resolved regions and to surfaces the user explicitly opened.
capabilities.rationale: A page that animates itself in on every navigation reads as slow regardless of how fast it actually is. This is the most common way motion makes a product feel worse rather than better.

capabilities.title: Motion explains what happened
capabilities.description: A transition communicates where an object went, what it became, or which action caused the change — rather than being decoration applied uniformly to every state change.
capabilities.rationale: The genuinely judgmental half of motion quality. Whether a shared-element transition actually preserved object identity for a human observer is not something a duration comparison can settle, so the ceiling is manual with expiry.
